# Authoring a Module

A module package keeps its shared Rust API at the root and places each Host
implementation beside it:

```text
whisker-toggle/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/lib.rs
├── android/src/main/kotlin/.../ToggleModule.kt
├── build.gradle.kts
├── ios/Sources/WhiskerToggle/ToggleModule.swift
├── Package.swift
├── desktop/Cargo.toml
├── desktop/src/lib.rs
├── web/Cargo.toml
└── web/src/lib.rs
```

Start with:

```sh
whisker new-module whisker-toggle
```

The generated module is a normal Cargo package. Check its sources in; module
implementations are authored code, not generated bindings.

## Package metadata

```toml
[package.metadata.whisker]

[package.metadata.whisker.desktop]
package = "whisker-toggle-desktop-host"

[package.metadata.whisker.web]
package = "whisker-toggle-web-host"
```

The empty marker makes the package discoverable. Desktop and Web name the Host
crates Cargo should select for those targets. Swift Package Manager and Gradle
resolve the mobile sources through `Package.swift` and `build.gradle.kts`.

## Declare a Host element in Rust

```rust
use whisker::{Signal, Style};
use whisker::event::CustomEvent;

#[whisker::module_element(
    name = "acme.toggle/Toggle",
    measurement = None,
    commands = [("setChecked", Bool)],
)]
pub fn toggle(
    checked: Signal<bool>,
    disabled: Signal<bool>,
    style: Style,
    on_change: CustomEvent,
) {
}
```

The macro creates the PascalCase `Toggle(...)` builder and an element schema.
Signal props can update after mount. Event props begin with `on_`. Commands are
one-way and accept one declared `WhiskerValue` shape.

Choose `measurement = None` for layout-determined elements and `Custom` when
the Host must report an intrinsic size, as text or an asynchronously loaded
image does. Whether an element accepts children is inferred from a `Children`
argument; Host-only child-container details remain in the Host implementation.

## Implement the same contract on each Host

The API shape is intentionally symmetric even though the registration
mechanism is native to each platform.

### Android

```kotlin
@WhiskerModule
class ToggleModule : Module() {
    override fun definition() = ModuleDefinition {
        Name("Toggle")
        View("acme.toggle/Toggle", ToggleView::class.java) {
            Prop("checked") { view: ToggleView, value ->
                view.setChecked(value.asBool() ?: false)
            }
            Events("change")
            Command("setChecked") { view: ToggleView, value ->
                view.setChecked(value.asBool() ?: false)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### iOS

```swift
@WhiskerModule
public final class ToggleModule: Module {
    public override func definition() -> ModuleDefinition {
        ModuleDefinition {
            Name("Toggle")
            View("acme.toggle/Toggle", ToggleView.self) {
                Prop("checked") { (view: ToggleView, value: WhiskerValue) in
                    view.setChecked(value.asBool ?? false)
                }
                Events("change")
                Command("setChecked") { (view: ToggleView, value: WhiskerValue) in
                    view.setChecked(value.asBool ?? false)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Desktop and Web define the same names with their Rust Host SDK builders. Host
code creates and updates only its own view. Whisker's root Host applies layout,
paint, clipping, accessibility, event routing, and child insertion from the
shared frame protocol.

## Service functions and events

Native definitions may also declare `Function`, `AsyncFunction`, `Events`, and
observation hooks. Wrap them in a typed Rust facade over `module!`:

```rust
pub async fn load(key: String) -> Result<WhiskerValue, String> {
    match whisker::module!("Store")
        .invoke_async("load", vec![WhiskerValue::String(key)])
        .await
    {
        WhiskerValue::Error(message) => Err(message),
        value => Ok(value),
    }
}
```

## Compatibility failures

The Rust schema and Host catalog are compared by name and value kind when the
Host starts. A missing element, property, event, or command is a clear runtime
registration error. Keep those names stable within a released major version
and test each Host against shared conformance fixtures.

# Authoring a Plugin

09aa265 chore: release 20261109.1 (#774)
Scaffold a new Whisker app — single-crate workspace with `Cargo.toml`, a `#[whisker::main]` `src/lib.rs`, the `whisker.rs` project generator, `.gitignore`, and `README.md`. The result compiles standalone; run `whisker run android` or `whisker run ios` from inside the new directory

Usage: whisker new [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  The cargo crate name. kebab-case (`my-app`, `awesome-thing`). Must be a valid cargo package name — letters / digits / `-` / `_`, must start with a letter

Options:
      --path <PATH>                  Optional parent directory. Defaults to the current working directory. The new crate lands at `<parent>/<name>/`
  -v, --verbose                      Show every step's full underlying output (raw cargo / xcodebuild / simctl streams + the internal debug logs the curated UI hides by default). Plumbed into `whisker-build::ui` via the `WHISKER_VERBOSE` env var so subprocesses (`whisker-dev-server`, the shim binaries, etc.) inherit it
      --bundle-id <BUNDLE_ID>        Override the iOS bundle id / Android applicationId. Defaults to `rs.example.<snake_case_name>`
      --no-tui                       Disable the inline progress UI for long-running build/run workflows. Plain deterministic output is always used when piping or under CI
      --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>  Override the human-readable app display name. Defaults to the crate name with `-` swapped for spaces and each word title-cased (`my-app` → `My App`)
  -h, --help                         Print help
Produce distributable, signed artifacts — `appbundle` (.aab), `apk` and `ipa`. Signing material comes from the encrypted `credentials/` store; missing pieces are set up interactively on first use

Usage: whisker build [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  appbundle  Android App Bundle (.aab), release-signed from the credentials/ store — the format Play Console accepts
  apk        Release-signed APK for direct distribution (Firebase App Distribution, internal testing, sideloading)
  ipa        iOS .ipa — `xcodebuild archive` + export, signed via the App Store Connect API key with Apple's cloud-managed distribution certificate. `--method ad-hoc` for device-limited distribution
  macos      Native macOS `.app` bundle built from the CNG-generated Cargo project
  windows    Windows executable and resources (unpackaged, unsigned)
  linux      Linux installation tree (bin/ and share/)
  web        Static browser bundle (`index.html`, JavaScript glue, and WebAssembly)
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose  Show every step's full underlying output (raw cargo / xcodebuild / simctl streams + the internal debug logs the curated UI hides by default). Plumbed into `whisker-build::ui` via the `WHISKER_VERBOSE` env var so subprocesses (`whisker-dev-server`, the shim binaries, etc.) inherit it
      --no-tui   Disable the inline progress UI for long-running build/run workflows. Plain deterministic output is always used when piping or under CI
  -h, --help     Print help
Scaffold a new Whisker module crate — Cargo.toml (with the `[package.metadata.whisker.module.platforms]` support map), Package.swift, build.gradle.kts, and skeleton Rust / Swift / Kotlin sources. See `docs/module-api-design.md`

Usage: whisker new-module [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>
          The cargo crate name. Convention: kebab-case, prefixed with `whisker-` (e.g. `whisker-camera`, `whisker-blur-view`). Must be a valid cargo package name — letters / digits / `-` / `_`, must start with a letter

Options:
      --path <PATH>
          Optional parent directory. Defaults to the current working directory. The new crate lands at `<parent>/<name>/`

  -v, --verbose
          Show every step's full underlying output (raw cargo / xcodebuild / simctl streams + the internal debug logs the curated UI hides by default). Plumbed into `whisker-build::ui` via the `WHISKER_VERBOSE` env var so subprocesses (`whisker-dev-server`, the shim binaries, etc.) inherit it

      --no-tui
          Disable the inline progress UI for long-running build/run workflows. Plain deterministic output is always used when piping or under CI

      --shape <SHAPE>
          Module shape. `view-bearing` (the default) generates a `#[whisker::module_element]` shim + a DSL module with a `View(...)` block and a `WhiskerUI<View>` subclass. `function-only` generates a `#[whisker::platform_module]` proxy + a DSL module with module-level `Function`s and no `View(...)` — for modules that only expose function calls (e.g. `whisker-local-store`-style key-value stores)

          Possible values:
          - view-bearing:  View-bearing — renders a native view + supports prop / method dispatch via `ElementRef<T>`
          - function-only: Function-only — Rust calls platform-side functions; no UI
          
          [default: view-bearing]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

content.content:
5754	is shown, where a `navigate` pushes — is _derived_ from these two graphs.
5755	
5756	```rust
5757	use whisker::prelude::*;
5758	use whisker_router::*;
5759	```
5760	
5761	For a step-by-step walkthrough, see the [Routing guide](/docs/routing.md).
5762	This page is the complete API reference.
5763	
5764	## Architecture overview
5765	
5766	```text
5767	┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
5768	│                      routes! { ... }                         │
5769	│                                                              │
5770	│   Declares the static route tree:                            │
5771	│   • Route — a screen or layout                               │
5772	│   • Stack — ordered container (push/pop history)             │
5773	│   • Switch — parallel container (keep-alive, select one)     │
5774	│                         │                                    │
5775	│                         ▼                                    │
5776	│                      RouteSet                                │
5777	│          (CompiledTree + RouteRegistry)                      │
5778	└──────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
5779	                           │
5780	                           ▼
5781	                  Router(routes: RouteSet)
5782	                           │
5783	                    ┌──────┴──────┐
5784	                    │ RouterHandle │  ← created internally; Clone to share
5785	                    └──────┬──────┘
5786	                           │
5787	              ┌────────────┼─────────────┐
5788	              ▼            ▼             ▼
5789	         navigate()    select()      back()  ...
5790	              │            │             │
5791	              └────────────┼─────────────┘
5792	                           │
5793	                           ▼
5794	                      RouteState
5795	                  (mutable, runtime)
5796	                           │
5797	                           ▼
5798	                     Outlet / Stack / Switch
5799	                   (render the active route)
5800	```
5801	
5802	| Layer      | Symbols                                                                                                     | Purpose                         |
5803	| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
5804	| Route tree | [`routes!`](#the-routes-macro)                                                                              | Declare the screen structure    |
5805	| Handle     | [`RouterHandle`](#routerhandle)                                                                             | Signal-backed navigation state  |
5806	| Context    | [`Router`](#router-component), [`use_navigator`](#hooks), [`use_param`](#hooks), [`use_pathname`](#hooks)   | Publish/read the router         |
5807	| Renderer   | [`Outlet`](#outlet), [`Stack`](#stack-renderer), [`Switch`](#switch-renderer), [`Layout`](#layout-renderer) | Turn state into UI              |
5808	| Animation  | [`RouteTransition`](#transitions)                                                                           | How screens enter/leave         |
5809	| Host input | Installed internally by [`Router`](#router-component)                                                       | Back, gestures, browser history |
5810	
5811	## The `routes!` macro
5812	
5813	`routes!` declares the full screen structure and produces a
5814	[`RouteSet`](#routeset). The grammar has three node types:
5815	
5816	### Route
5817	
5818	A screen or layout. Takes named keyword arguments:
5819	
5820	```rust
5821	Route(path: "detail/:id", component: Detail)
5822	Route(path: "detail/:id", component: Detail, transition: RouteTransition::modal())
5823	```
5824	
5825	| Parameter    | Required                 | Description                                                            |
5826	| ------------ | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
5827	| `path`       | Yes (unless layout-only) | URL segment. `:name` for dynamic params. `(name)` for group segments   |
5828	| `component`  | No                       | The `#[component]` to render                                           |
5829	| `transition` | No                       | A [`RouteTransition`](#transitions) override (default: platform slide) |
5830	
5831	A `Route` with **both** a `component` and children is a **layout
5832	route** — its component must render an `Outlet` for children to appear.
5833	See [Route nesting](#route-nesting).
5834	
5835	A `Route` with a parenthesised path like `(home)` is a **group route**:
5836	the segment appears in the canonical URL but is optional during
5837	matching. Use groups to organize Switch branches without forcing URLs.
5838	
5839	### Stack
5840	
5841	An ordered container with push/pop history. Its children are `Route`
5842	nodes (or `..spread` fragments):
5843	
5844	```rust
5845	Stack {
5846	    Route(path: "", component: Home)
5847	    Route(path: "detail/:id", component: Detail)
5848	}
5849	```
5850	
5851	`navigate()` pushes onto the active Stack; `back()` pops it.
5852	
5853	### Switch
5854	
5855	A parallel container. All branches are kept alive; one is selected:
5856	
5857	```rust
5858	Switch {
5859	    Route(path: "(home)") {
5860	        Stack { ... }
5861	    }
5862	    Route(path: "(search)") {
5863	        Stack { ... }
5864	    }
5865	}
5866	```
5867	
5868	`select()` changes the active branch. `back()` never changes Switch
5869	selection — it only pops Stacks.
5870	
5871	### Spread
5872	
5873	Reusable route fragments can be spread into containers:
5874	
5875	```rust
5876	let shared = routes! {
5877	    Route(path: "post/:id", component: Post)
5878	    Route(path: "profile/:id", component: Profile)
5879	};
5880	
5881	let app = routes! {
5882	    Stack {
5883	        Route(path: "", component: Home)
5884	        ..shared
5885	    }
5886	};
5887	```
5888	
5889	### Full example
5890	
5891	```rust
5892	routes! {
5893	    Route(component: TabsLayout) {
5894	        Switch {
5895	            Route(path: "(home)") {
5896	                Stack {
5897	                    Route(path: "", component: Timeline)
5898	                    Route(path: "post/:id", component: Post)
5899	                }
5900	            }
5901	            Route(path: "(search)") {
5902	                Stack {
5903	                    Route(path: "search", component: Search)
5904	                    Route(path: "post/:id", component: Post)
5905	                }
5906	            }
5907	        }
5908	    }
5909	    Route(path: "video/:id", component: VideoPlayer,
5910	          transition: RouteTransition::modal())
5911	}
5912	```
5913	
5914	## Route nesting
5915	
5916	Nesting a `Route` inside another `Route` creates a **layout
5917	relationship**, not a pushable screen. The parent must render an
5918	`Outlet` for the child to appear.
5919	
5920	```text
5921	 ┌─ Stack ──────────────────────┐       ┌─ Stack ──────────────────────┐
5922	 │                              │       │                              │
5923	 │  Route(Home)                 │       │  Route(Home)                 │
5924	 │    └── Route(Detail)  ✗     │       │  Route(Detail)         ✓    │
5925	 │                              │       │                              │
5926	 │  Detail is a CHILD of Home.  │       │  Detail is a SIBLING.        │
5927	 │  navigate() modifies         │       │  navigate() pushes Detail    │
5928	 │  child state in-place.       │       │  onto the Stack.             │
5929	 │  back() does not pop.        │       │  back() pops to Home.        │
5930	 └──────────────────────────────┘       └──────────────────────────────┘
5931	```
5932	
5933	Reserve Route nesting for layout routes (tab bar, header chrome) where
5934	the parent renders shared UI around an `Outlet`.
5935	
5936	## URL derivation
5937	
5938	A Route's URL is the concatenation of all segments from root to leaf.
5939	Containers (`Stack`/`Switch`) contribute nothing.
5940	
5941	```text
5942	Route(component: TabsLayout)           → (no segment)
5943	  └─ Switch                            → (no segment)
5944	       └─ Route(path: "(home)")        → /(home)
5945	            └─ Stack                   → (no segment)
5946	                 └─ Route("detail/:id") → /(home)/detail/:id
5947	```
5948	
5949	Group segments `(name)` appear in canonical URLs but are skipped during
5950	matching: `navigate("/detail/42")` matches `/(home)/detail/:id`.
5951	
5952	## RouteSet
5953	
5954	The output of `routes!`. Contains:
5955	
5956	- A `CompiledTree` — the static tree with pre-computed URLs and node paths
5957	- A `RouteRegistry` — the id → render-function + transition map
5958	- A `LayoutRegistry` — layout route → component map
5959	
5960	Construct manually with `RouteSet::from_parts(tree, registry)` for the
5961	rare hand-built case.
5962	
5963	## RouterHandle
5964	
5965	The signal-backed navigation handle. Owns the immutable tree, registry,
5966	and a single `RwSignal<RouteState>`. `Clone` shares the same underlying
5967	state (it is `Rc`-backed).
5968	
5969	### Construction
5970	
5971	`Router` creates the handle internally from the `routes` you pass it, so
5972	most apps never construct a `RouterHandle` directly:
5973	
5974	```rust
5975	// Most apps: Router creates the handle internally
5976	Router(routes: routes! { ... }) { ... }
5977	
5978	// Advanced: create the handle manually for pre-mount logic
5979	let handle = RouterHandle::new(routes! { ... });
5980	```
5981	
5982	When you build the handle yourself, publish it with
5983	`provide_router(handle)` instead of passing `routes` to `Router`.
5984	
5985	### Navigation operations
5986	
5987	All targets are plain `&str` URLs. Returns `Result<(), NavError>`.
5988	
5989	| Method          | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
5990	| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
5991	| `navigate(url)` | Push the matched route onto the active Stack. Always pushes — no dedup                                                                                                                                                                   |
5992	| `select(url)`   | Select the Switch branch containing the target (tab switching)                                                                                                                                                                           |
5993	| `back()`        | Pop the deepest non-trivial Stack. `NothingToPop` at root                                                                                                                                                                                |
5994	| `replace(url)`  | Swap the top of the current Stack (same-Stack only)                                                                                                                                                                                      |
5995	| `pop_to(url)`   | Pop until the target is on top (same-Stack only)                                                                                                                                                                                         |
5996	| `reset(url)`    | **Global**: rebuild the whole state onto a single clean path to the target — select every Switch toward it and collapse _every_ Stack to one entry, so **no back history survives anywhere** (on the target path or in any other branch) |
5997	
5998	```rust
5999	let nav = use_navigator();
6000	nav.navigate("/detail/42");    // push
6001	nav.select("/(search)");      // switch tab
6002	nav.replace("/detail/99");     // swap top
6003	nav.back();                    // pop
6004	nav.pop_to("/");               // pop to root
6005	nav.reset("/");                // clear EVERY back stack, go to Home
6006	```
6007	
6008	> **`reset` is global, the others are same-Stack.** `replace` / `pop_to`
6009	> operate only on the current Stack. `reset` is the "clean slate" verb
6010	> (logout, post-login): it resolves the target anywhere in the tree (like
6011	> `navigate`), switches tabs toward it, and clears the back stack of _every_
6012	> Stack — not just the current one. Equivalent to React Navigation's
6013	> `reset({ routes })` or Flutter's `pushAndRemoveUntil(_, (_) => false)`.
6014	
6015	### NavError
6016	
6017	| Variant        | Meaning                                |
6018	| -------------- | -------------------------------------- |
6019	| `NoSuchTarget` | URL matches no route in the tree       |
6020	| `NothingToPop` | `back()` at a root with nothing to pop |
6021	
6022	### Resolution rule
6023	
6024	A URL always resolves to a **leaf screen** — never a container (a `Stack`,
6025	`Switch`, or `(group)`). Group segments in the URL are **optional**, so both
6026	`/detail/42` and `/(home)/detail/42` match the pattern `/(home)/detail/:id`.
6027	
6028	| URL                               | Resolves to                                                               |
6029	| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
6030	| `/`                               | The home **index** screen — the `""` route, reached even from another tab |
6031	| `/(home)`                         | The home tab's index screen (same as `/` here)                            |
6032	| `/(search)`                       | The search tab's **first** screen (its group has no `""` index)           |
6033	| `/list`, `/(search)/list`         | The `list` screen (group optional)                                        |
6034	| `/detail/42`, `/(home)/detail/42` | The `detail` screen with `id = 42`                                        |
6035	
6036	When a URL matches **multiple** positions (e.g. a shared `post/:id` in both
6037	tabs), relative resolution picks the instance sharing the **deepest common
6038	ancestor with the current position**. Ties break by **declaration order**
6039	(first defined wins).
6040	
6041	| Situation                          | Resolves to        | Why                     |
6042	| ---------------------------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------- |
6043	| From tab A, `navigate("/post/42")` | Tab A's `post/:id` | Deepest common ancestor |
6044	| From tab B, `navigate("/post/42")` | Tab B's `post/:id` | Within tab B's subtree  |
6045	| From outside tabs                  | First declared     | Common ancestor is root |
6046	
6047	## Router component
6048	
6049	Takes a `RouteSet`, creates the `RouterHandle` internally, publishes it
6050	into context, creates a positioned root view, and installs the current Host's
6051	navigation driver. Mount renderers and application chrome as children:
6052	
6053	```rust
6054	Router(routes: routes! {
6055	    Stack {
6056	        Route(path: "", component: Home)
6057	        Route(path: "detail/:id", component: Detail)
6058	    }
6059	}) {
6060	    Outlet {}
6061	}
6062	```
6063	
6064	| Prop       | Type       | Notes                                |
6065	| ---------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
6066	| `routes`   | `RouteSet` | The route tree (output of `routes!`) |
6067	| `children` | `Children` | Renderers + application chrome       |
6068	
6069	## Renderers
6070	
6071	Renderers turn the current `RouteState` into UI. They are mounted
6072	inside a `Router` (or inside a layout route's `Outlet`).
6073	
6074	### Outlet
6075	
6076	Renders the active route at the current anchor point. In a layout
6077	route's component, `Outlet` renders that route's active child:
6078	
6079	```rust
6080	#[component]
6081	fn tabs_layout() -> Element {
6082	    render! {
6083	        View(style: css!(flex_grow: 1.0)) {
6084	            Outlet {}     // renders the active child
6085	        }
6086	        MyTabBar {}       // persistent chrome
6087	    }
6088	}
6089	```
6090

6143

## Architecture overview

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      routes! { ... }                         │
│                                                              │
│   Declares the static route tree:                            │
│   • Route — a screen or layout                               │
│   • Stack — ordered container (push/pop history)             │
│   • Switch — parallel container (keep-alive, select one)     │
│                         │                                    │
│                         ▼                                    │
│                      RouteSet                                │
│          (CompiledTree + RouteRegistry)                      │
└──────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
                  Router(routes: RouteSet)
                           │
                    ┌──────┴──────┐
                    │ RouterHandle │  ← created internally; Clone to share
                    └──────┬──────┘
                           │
              ┌────────────┼─────────────┐
              ▼            ▼             ▼
         navigate()    select()      back()  ...
              │            │             │
              └────────────┼─────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
                      RouteState
                  (mutable, runtime)
                           │
                           ▼
                     Outlet / Stack / Switch
                   (render the active route)
```

| Layer      | Symbols                                                                                                     | Purpose                         |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Route tree | [`routes!`](#the-routes-macro)                                                                              | Declare the screen structure    |
| Handle     | [`RouterHandle`](#routerhandle)                                                                             | Signal-backed navigation state  |
| Context    | [`Router`](#router-component), [`use_navigator`](#hooks), [`use_param`](#hooks), [`use_pathname`](#hooks)   | Publish/read the router         |
| Renderer   | [`Outlet`](#outlet), [`Stack`](#stack-renderer), [`Switch`](#switch-renderer), [`Layout`](#layout-renderer) | Turn state into UI              |
| Animation  | [`RouteTransition`](#transitions)                                                                           | How screens enter/leave         |
| Host input | Installed internally by [`Router`](#router-component)                                                       | Back, gestures, browser history |

## The `routes!` macro

`routes!` declares the full screen structure and produces a
[`RouteSet`](#routeset). The grammar has three node types:

### Route

A screen or layout. Takes named keyword arguments:

```rust
Route(path: "detail/:id", component: Detail)
Route(path: "detail/:id", component: Detail, transition: RouteTransition::modal())
```

| Parameter    | Required                 | Description                                                            |
| ------------ | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`       | Yes (unless layout-only) | URL segment. `:name` for dynamic params. `(name)` for group segments   |
| `component`  | No                       | The `#[component]` to render                                           |
| `transition` | No                       | A [`RouteTransition`](#transitions) override (default: platform slide) |

A `Route` with **both** a `component` and children is a **layout
route** — its component must render an `Outlet` for children to appear.
See [Route nesting](#route-nesting).

A `Route` with a parenthesised path like `(home)` is a **group route**:
the segment appears in the canonical URL but is optional during
matching. Use groups to organize Switch branches without forcing URLs.

### Stack

An ordered container with push/pop history. Its children are `Route`
nodes (or `..spread` fragments):

```rust
Stack {
    Route(path: "", component: Home)
    Route(path: "detail/:id", component: Detail)
}
```

`navigate()` pushes onto the active Stack; `back()` pops it.

### Switch

A parallel container. All branches are kept alive; one is selected:

```rust
Switch {
    Route(path: "(home)") {
        Stack { ... }
    }
    Route(path: "(search)") {
        Stack { ... }
    }
}
```

`select()` changes the active branch. `back()` never changes Switch
selection — it only pops Stacks.

### Spread

Reusable route fragments can be spread into containers:

```rust
let shared = routes! {
    Route(path: "post/:id", component: Post)
    Route(path: "profile/:id", component: Profile)
};

let app = routes! {
    Stack {
        Route(path: "", component: Home)
        ..shared
    }
};
```

### Full example

```rust
routes! {
    Route(component: TabsLayout) {
        Switch {
            Route(path: "(home)") {
                Stack {
                    Route(path: "", component: Timeline)
                    Route(path: "post/:id", component: Post)
                }
            }
            Route(path: "(search)") {
                Stack {
                    Route(path: "search", component: Search)
                    Route(path: "post/:id", component: Post)
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Route(path: "video/:id", component: VideoPlayer,
          transition: RouteTransition::modal())
}
```

## Route nesting

Nesting a `Route` inside another `Route` creates a **layout
relationship**, not a pushable screen. The parent must render an
`Outlet` for the child to appear.

```text
 ┌─ Stack ──────────────────────┐       ┌─ Stack ──────────────────────┐
 │                              │       │                              │
 │  Route(Home)                 │       │  Route(Home)                 │
 │    └── Route(Detail)  ✗     │       │  Route(Detail)         ✓    │
 │                              │       │                              │
 │  Detail is a CHILD of Home.  │       │  Detail is a SIBLING.        │
 │  navigate() modifies         │       │  navigate() pushes Detail    │
 │  child state in-place.       │       │  onto the Stack.             │
 │  back() does not pop.        │       │  back() pops to Home.        │
 └──────────────────────────────┘       └──────────────────────────────┘
```

Reserve Route nesting for layout routes (tab bar, header chrome) where
the parent renders shared UI around an `Outlet`.

## URL derivation

A Route's URL is the concatenation of all segments from root to leaf.
Containers (`Stack`/`Switch`) contribute nothing.

```text
Route(component: TabsLayout)           → (no segment)
  └─ Switch                            → (no segment)
       └─ Route(path: "(home)")        → /(home)
            └─ Stack                   → (no segment)
                 └─ Route("detail/:id") → /(home)/detail/:id
```

Group segments `(name)` appear in canonical URLs but are skipped during
matching: `navigate("/detail/42")` matches `/(home)/detail/:id`.

## RouteSet

The output of `routes!`. Contains:

- A `CompiledTree` — the static tree with pre-computed URLs and node paths
- A `RouteRegistry` — the id → render-function + transition map
- A `LayoutRegistry` — layout route → component map

Construct manually with `RouteSet::from_parts(tree, registry)` for the
rare hand-built case.

## RouterHandle

The signal-backed navigation handle. Owns the immutable tree, registry,
and a single `RwSignal<RouteState>`. `Clone` shares the same underlying
state (it is `Rc`-backed).

### Construction

`Router` creates the handle internally from the `routes` you pass it, so
most apps never construct a `RouterHandle` directly:

```rust
// Most apps: Router creates the handle internally
Router(routes: routes! { ... }) { ... }

// Advanced: create the handle manually for pre-mount logic
let handle = RouterHandle::new(routes! { ... });
```

When you build the handle yourself, publish it with
`provide_router(handle)` instead of passing `routes` to `Router`.

### Navigation operations

All targets are plain `&str` URLs. Returns `Result<(), NavError>`.

| Method          | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `navigate(url)` | Push the matched route onto the active Stack. Always pushes — no dedup                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `select(url)`   | Select the Switch branch containing the target (tab switching)                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `back()`        | Pop the deepest non-trivial Stack. `NothingToPop` at root                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `replace(url)`  | Swap the top of the current Stack (same-Stack only)                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `pop_to(url)`   | Pop until the target is on top (same-Stack only)                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `reset(url)`    | **Global**: rebuild the whole state onto a single clean path to the target — select every Switch toward it and collapse _every_ Stack to one entry, so **no back history survives anywhere** (on the target path or in any other branch) |

```rust
let nav = use_navigator();
nav.navigate("/detail/42");    // push
nav.select("/(search)");      // switch tab
nav.replace("/detail/99");     // swap top
nav.back();                    // pop
nav.pop_to("/");               // pop to root
nav.reset("/");                // clear EVERY back stack, go to Home
```

> **`reset` is global, the others are same-Stack.** `replace` / `pop_to`
> operate only on the current Stack. `reset` is the "clean slate" verb
> (logout, post-login): it resolves the target anywhere in the tree (like
> `navigate`), switches tabs toward it, and clears the back stack of _every_
> Stack — not just the current one. Equivalent to React Navigation's
> `reset({ routes })` or Flutter's `pushAndRemoveUntil(_, (_) => false)`.

### NavError

| Variant        | Meaning                                |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `NoSuchTarget` | URL matches no route in the tree       |
| `NothingToPop` | `back()` at a root with nothing to pop |

### Resolution rule

A URL always resolves to a **leaf screen** — never a container (a `Stack`,
`Switch`, or `(group)`). Group segments in the URL are **optional**, so both
`/detail/42` and `/(home)/detail/42` match the pattern `/(home)/detail/:id`.

| URL                               | Resolves to                                                               |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/`                               | The home **index** screen — the `""` route, reached even from another tab |
| `/(home)`                         | The home tab's index screen (same as `/` here)                            |
| `/(search)`                       | The search tab's **first** screen (its group has no `""` index)           |
| `/list`, `/(search)/list`         | The `list` screen (group optional)                                        |
| `/detail/42`, `/(home)/detail/42` | The `detail` screen with `id = 42`                                        |

When a URL matches **multiple** positions (e.g. a shared `post/:id` in both
tabs), relative resolution picks the instance sharing the **deepest common
ancestor with the current position**. Ties break by **declaration order**
(first defined wins).

| Situation                          | Resolves to        | Why                     |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------- |
| From tab A, `navigate("/post/42")` | Tab A's `post/:id` | Deepest common ancestor |
| From tab B, `navigate("/post/42")` | Tab B's `post/:id` | Within tab B's subtree  |
| From outside tabs                  | First declared     | Common ancestor is root |

## Router component

Takes a `RouteSet`, creates the `RouterHandle` internally, publishes it
into context, creates a positioned root view, and installs the current Host's
navigation driver. Mount renderers and application chrome as children:

```rust
Router(routes: routes! {
    Stack {
        Route(path: "", component: Home)
        Route(path: "detail/:id", component: Detail)
    }
}) {
    Outlet {}
}
```

| Prop       | Type       | Notes                                |
| ---------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `routes`   | `RouteSet` | The route tree (output of `routes!`) |
| `children` | `Children` | Renderers + application chrome       |

## Renderers

Renderers turn the current `RouteState` into UI. They are mounted
inside a `Router` (or inside a layout route's `Outlet`).

### Outlet

Renders the active route at the current anchor point. In a layout
route's component, `Outlet` renders that route's active child:

```rust
#[component]
fn tabs_layout() -> Element {
    render! {
        View(style: css!(flex_grow: 1.0)) {
            Outlet {}     // renders the active child
        }
        MyTabBar {}       // persistent chrome
    }
}
```

No props. `Outlet` reads the router context and the current anchor
path to determine what to render.

### Stack renderer

The `Stack` renderer handles Stack containers: it manages push/pop
history with screen-preserving wrappers and coordinated transitions.

### Switch renderer

The `Switch` renderer handles Switch containers: it keeps all branches
mounted and toggles visibility based on the selected branch.

### Layout renderer

The `Layout` renderer handles layout routes: it renders the layout
component (which must contain an `Outlet`) and passes children through.

## Transitions

A `RouteTransition` defines how a route enters and leaves its Stack.
Transitions are **parameters of the `Route`**, not the component —
the same component can have different transitions at different Route
sites.

### Built-in transitions

| Constructor                     | Description                                                    |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RouteTransition::slide()`      | iOS-style horizontal slide with parallax and dim (iOS default) |
| `RouteTransition::slide_fade()` | Subtle horizontal slide + fade (Android default)               |
| `RouteTransition::fade()`       | Cross-fade opacity                                             |
| `RouteTransition::modal()`      | Slide up from the bottom                                       |
| `RouteTransition::none()`       | No animation — instant swap                                    |

The default is **platform-aware**: `slide()` on iOS, `slide_fade()`
on Android.

### Per-route transition

```rust
routes! {
    Stack {
        Route(path: "", component: Home)
        Route(path: "detail/:id", component: Detail)
        Route(path: "compose", component: Compose,
              transition: RouteTransition::modal())
    }
}
```

### Custom transitions

Implement the `Transition` trait and wrap with `RouteTransition::custom`:

```rust
struct ZoomIn;

impl Transition for ZoomIn {
    fn config(&self) -> AnimConfig {
        AnimConfig::new(300, "ease-out")
    }

    fn pose(&self, ctx: PoseContext) -> Pose {
        match ctx.role {
            Role::Top => {
                let scale = 0.85 + 0.15 * ctx.progress;
                Pose::new(
                    format!("scale({})", scale),
                    ctx.progress,  // opacity
                )
            }
            Role::Under => Pose::new(String::new(), 1.0),
        }
    }
}

Route(path: "preview", component: Preview,
      transition: RouteTransition::custom(ZoomIn))
```

### Transition types

| Type                 | Description                                           |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `RouteTransition`    | `Rc`-backed wrapper (cheap to Clone)                  |
| `Transition` (trait) | `config()` + `pose(PoseContext) -> Pose`              |
| `PoseContext`        | `{ role: Role, progress: f32, direction: Direction }` |
| `Pose`               | `{ transform: String, opacity: f32, radius_px: f32 }` |
| `Role`               | `Top` (entering/leaving) or `Under` (beneath)         |
| `Direction`          | `Push` (forward) or `Pop` (back)                      |
| `AnimConfig`         | Duration (ms) + easing function                       |

### Progress convention

`progress` is "how present the top screen is":

- `1.0` → top screen fully on screen
- `0.0` → top screen fully off screen

A **push** drives `0.0 → 1.0`; a **pop** drives `1.0 → 0.0`. One
controller drives both the Top and Under wrappers — the "gesture spans
two routes" problem solved by composition.

## Platform navigation drivers

`Router` installs Host navigation input automatically. There is no empty
gesture component to import or mount.

| Platform | Input                                                                                                |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Android  | System back on all supported versions; predictive-back progress and Material preview where available |
| iOS      | Left-edge interactive swipe back                                                                     |
| Web      | Initial URL plus browser back/forward through the History API                                        |
| Desktop  | No Host navigation input; use `RouterHandle` operations                                              |

Interactive inputs drive the Router's common coordinated two-screen
controller. Android predictive back uses its Material card pose, while iOS

The Android predictive back implements the full Material shared-element

radius, and shifts toward the swipe edge. On commit, the card fades and
the previous screen slides in.

## Modals

A modal is an ordinary `Route` with a modal transition:

```rust
Route(path: "compose", component: Compose,
      transition: RouteTransition::modal())
```

It stacks normally — `navigate("/compose")` pushes it, `back()` pops
it. The transition changes only the animation (slide-up), not the
semantics. Place modals as children of the root Stack (above the tabs

6340

6379	## `whisker-svg`
6380	
6381	Inline SVG widget. Compiles SVG XML to a display-list byte stream in
6382	Rust, then streams it to a native replayer.
6383	
6384	```toml
6385	[dependencies]
6386	whisker-svg = "0.12"
6387	```
6388	
6389	### `Svg`
6390	
6391	A pure component (declared with `#[component]`, wrapping an internal
6392	module element).
6393	
6394	| Prop      | Type             | Notes                                                                                                                                    |
6395	| --------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
6396	| `content` | `Signal<String>` | SVG XML source. Must contain a top-level `<svg>` with a `viewBox`. Empty string renders nothing. A content swap recompiles + re-renders. |
6397	| `color`   | `Signal<String>` | CSS color applied to any `fill="currentColor"` / `stroke="currentColor"` paint.                                                          |
6398	| `style`   | `Style`          | Structured style. Width/height may be explicit or supplied by layout.                                                                    |
6399	
6400	```rust
6401	use whisker_svg::Svg;
6402	
6403	render! {
6404	    Svg(
6405	        content: r#"<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">
6406	            <path d="M 5 12 L 10 17 L 19 7"
6407	                  stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/>
6408	        </svg>"#,
6409	        color: "#1d9bf0",
6410	        style: css!(width: px(24), height: px(24)),
6411	    )
6412	}
6413	```
6414	
6415	### Advanced: the compiler surface
6416	
6417	For callers who want to drive the compiler directly, the crate
6418	re-exports the display-list pipeline:
6419	
6420	| Symbol                                                | Purpose                                                                                 |
6421	| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
6422	| `compile`                                             | Compile SVG XML to a `Compiled` display list. Returns `Result<Compiled, CompileError>`. |
6423	| `Compiled` / `CompileError`                           | The success value (carries `bytes` + `warnings`) and the error type.                    |
6424	| `Color` / `DisplayListBuilder` / `Transform`          | Lower-level builder pieces for constructing a display list by hand.                     |
6425	| `replay` / `ReplayError` / `Visitor` / `TraceVisitor` | Walk a compiled display list, dispatching ops to a `Visitor`.                           |
6426	
6427	Most apps never touch these — use `Svg` (or [`whisker-icons`](#whisker-icons))
6428	instead.

6430	## `whisker-icons`
6431	
6432	Lucide icon set as a Whisker component. Each icon is its own
6433	`pub const &str`, so unreferenced icons are linker-DCE'd from your
6434	binary (tree shaking).
6435	
6436	```toml
6437	[dependencies]
6438	whisker-icons = "0.12"
6439	```
6440	
6441	### `Icon`
6442	
6443	A pure component that forwards to [`whisker_svg::Svg`](#whisker-svg).
6444	
6445	| Prop    | Type             | Notes                                                                                                                 |
6446	| ------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
6447	| `svg`   | `Signal<String>` | The SVG XML to render — usually a `lucide` constant.                                                                  |
6448	| `color` | `Signal<String>` | CSS color used as the `currentColor` substitution (Lucide draws with `stroke="currentColor"`).                        |
6449	| `size`  | `Signal<String>` | Square edge length. Bare numbers (`"24"`) are treated as `px`; values with a unit (`"1.5em"`, `"100%"`) pass through. |
6450	
6451	### `lucide`
6452	
6453	A module of ~1700 PascalCase `pub const &str` icon constants
6454	(`Heart`, `ChevronRight`, `Search`, `X`, `AlarmClock`, …), each holding
6455	the full Lucide SVG markup. Reference a constant by name and pass it to
6456	`Icon`'s `svg` prop.
6457	
6458	```rust
6459	use whisker_icons::{Icon, lucide};
6460	
6461	render! {
6462	    Icon(svg: lucide::Heart, color: "#ff5577", size: "24")
6463	}
6464	```
6465	
6466	## `whisker-video`
6467	
6468	Video playback element with imperative controls. A native UI element
6469	(`Video`) plus a typed handle (`VideoHandle`) bound on mount via
6470	[`element_ref:`](/docs/refs.md).
6471	
6472	```toml
6473	[dependencies]
6474	whisker-video = "0.12"
6475	```
6476	
6477	### `Video`
6478	
6479	Declared via `#[whisker::module_element(...)]`.
6480	
6481	| Prop          | Type             | Notes                                               |
6482	| ------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
6483	| `src`         | `Signal<String>` | Media URL.                                          |
6484	| `style`       | `Style`          | Structured layout and paint.                        |
6485	| `element_ref` | `ElementRef`     | Pass `handle.r()` to bind a `VideoHandle` on mount. |
6486	
6487	### `VideoHandle`
6488	
6489	A `Copy` handle wrapping an [`ElementRef`](/docs/refs.md). Each method
6490	dispatches a fire-and-forget call to the native player.
6491	
6492	| Method  | Signature                          | Effect                                                    |
6493	| ------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
6494	| `new`   | `fn() -> VideoHandle`              | Allocate a fresh, unbound handle.                         |
6495	| `r`     | `fn(&self) -> ElementRef`          | The `ElementRef` to pass to `Video(element_ref: …)`.      |
6496	| `play`  | `fn(&self)`                        | Start or resume playback from the current position.       |
6497	| `pause` | `fn(&self)`                        | Pause at the current position.                            |
6498	| `seek`  | `fn(&self, position_seconds: f64)` | Seek to an absolute position (seconds; clamped natively). |
6499	
6500	`VideoHandle` is `Copy`, so each `move ||` closure captures its own
6501	copy — no `clone()`.
6502	
6503	```rust
6504	use whisker_video::{Video, VideoHandle};
6505	
6506	let video = VideoHandle::new();
6507	
6508	render! {
6509	    View(style: css!(flex_direction: FlexDirection::Column)) {
6510	        Video(element_ref: video.r(), src: "https://example.com/clip.mp4",
6511	              style: css!(width: percent(100), height: px(240)))
6512	        View(style: css!(flex_direction: FlexDirection::Row)) {
6513	            Text(value: "play",  on_tap: move |_| video.play())
6514	            Text(value: "pause", on_tap: move |_| video.pause())
6515	            Text(value: "+10s",  on_tap: move |_| video.seek(10.0))
6516	        }
6517	    }
6518	}
6519	```
6520	
6521	## `whisker-audio`
6522	
6523	View-less audio playback. A `Player` handle drives the engine and
6524	exposes a reactive [`PlaybackStatus`](/docs/reactivity-api.md) signal. The
6525	crate also ships a plugin that contributes the iOS/Android permission
6526	and background-mode entries.
6527	
6528	```toml
6529	[dependencies]
6530	whisker-audio = "0.12"
6531	```
6532	
6533	### `Player`
6534	
6535	A `Clone` handle (internally `Rc`-counted); the native player releases
6536	when the last clone drops. Methods are fire-and-forget — state changes
6537	surface through `status()`, not return values.
6538	
6539	| Method       | Signature                                 | Effect                                                                          |
6540	| ------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
6541	| `new`        | `fn(source: impl Into<String>) -> Player` | Construct a player loading from `source` (HTTP/HTTPS or `file://`).             |
6542	| `play`       | `fn(&self)`                               | Start or resume playback.                                                       |
6543	| `pause`      | `fn(&self)`                               | Pause at the current position.                                                  |
6544	| `stop`       | `fn(&self)`                               | Stop and rewind to position 0 (stays loaded).                                   |
6545	| `seek_to`    | `fn(&self, position_seconds: f64)`        | Seek to an absolute position (seconds; clamped natively).                       |
6546	| `set_source` | `fn(&self, source: impl Into<String>)`    | Replace the loaded media (resets the player; empty string releases the source). |
6547	| `set_volume` | `fn(&self, value: f64)`                   | Set output gain on `[0.0, 1.0]` (clamped natively).                             |
6548	| `set_loop`   | `fn(&self, looping: bool)`                | Loop the source at end-of-media.                                                |
6549	| `status`     | `fn(&self) -> ReadSignal<PlaybackStatus>` | Reactive playback status. All clones share one signal.                          |
6550	
6551	### `PlaybackStatus`
6552	
6553	`#[non_exhaustive]` snapshot pushed by the native side (times in
6554	seconds). Read fields directly; construct only via the native module.
6555	
6556	| Field        | Type   | Meaning                                                                 |
6557	| ------------ | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
6558	| `position`   | `f64`  | Current playback position from the start.                               |
6559	| `duration`   | `f64`  | Total media duration. `0.0` while loading or for live streams.          |
6560	| `is_loaded`  | `bool` | `true` once the source headers are parsed and `duration` is meaningful. |
6561	| `is_playing` | `bool` | `true` while audio is actively playing.                                 |
6562	
6563	```rust
6564	use whisker_audio::Player;
6565	
6566	let player = Player::new("https://example.com/clip.mp3");
6567	let status = player.status();
6568	
6569	render! {
6570	    View(style: css!(flex_direction: FlexDirection::Column, padding: px(16))) {
6571	        Text(value: computed(move || format!(
6572	            "{:.1}s / {:.1}s",
6573	            status.get().position,
6574	            status.get().duration,
6575	        )))
6576	        View(on_tap: {
6577	            let p = player.clone();
6578	            move |_| p.play()
6579	        }) { Text(value: "play") }
6580	    }
6581	}
6582	```
6583	
6584	### Plugin: `WhiskerAudio` + `WhiskerAudioConfig`
6585	
6586	To record audio or keep playback alive in the background, register the
6587	plugin in `whisker.rs` (see [Configuration](/docs/configuration-api.md)).
6588	The plugin contributes the matching `Info.plist` /
6589	`AndroidManifest.xml` entries.
6590	
6591	| Config field / setter         | Type             | Effect                                                                                  |
6592	| ----------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
6593	| `microphone_permission`       | `Option<String>` | Sets `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` (iOS). Required before `AVAudioSession` can record. |
6594	| `record_audio_android`        | `bool`           | Appends `android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO` to the Android manifest. Default `false`.     |
6595	| `enable_background_recording` | `bool`           | Adds `"audio"` to iOS `UIBackgroundModes`. Default `false`.                             |
6596	| `enable_background_playback`  | `bool`           | Same `UIBackgroundModes` entry, expressing playback intent. Default `false`.            |
6597	
6598	```rust
6599	use whisker_audio::WhiskerAudio;
6600	
6601	app.plugin::<WhiskerAudio>(|c| c
6602	    .microphone_permission("Record audio clips for podcasts.")
6603	    .record_audio_android(true)
6604	    .enable_background_playback(true));
6605	```
6606	
6607	## `whisker-safe-area`
6608	
6609	Reactive accessor for the host view's safe-area insets (notch, Dynamic
6610	Island, status bar, home indicator, navigation bar).
6611	
6612	```toml
6613	[dependencies]
6614	whisker-safe-area = "0.12"
6615	```
6616	
6617	### `safe_area_insets()`
6618	
6619	```rust
6620	pub fn safe_area_insets() -> ReadSignal<SafeAreaInsets>
6621	```
6622	
6623	Returns a process-global [`ReadSignal`](/docs/reactivity-api.md) wired to
6624	the native event on first call. Every call hands back the same
6625	underlying signal, so reading from many components is cheap. **Must be
6626	called from the main thread.**
6627	
6628	### `SafeAreaInsets`
6629	
6630	A `Copy` struct of inset amounts in points (iOS) / dp (Android) — the
6631	same units as Whisker's CSS `px` literals.
6632	
6633	| Field      | Type  | Meaning                             |
6634	| ---------- | ----- | ----------------------------------- |
6635	| `top`      | `f64` | Top inset.                          |
6636	| `leading`  | `f64` | Leading edge (`== left` for LTR).   |
6637	| `trailing` | `f64` | Trailing edge (`== right` for LTR). |
6638	| `bottom`   | `f64` | Bottom inset.                       |
6639	
6640	```rust
6641	use whisker_safe_area::safe_area_insets;
6642	
6643	let insets = safe_area_insets();
6644	let outer_style = move || {
6645	    let i = insets.get();
6646	    format!(
6647	        "padding-top: {}px; padding-bottom: {}px; \
6648	         padding-left: {}px; padding-right: {}px;",
6649	        i.top, i.bottom, i.leading, i.trailing,
6650	    )
6651	};
6652	
6653	render! {
6654	    View(style: outer_style()) {
6655	        // ...
6656	    }
6657	}
6658	```
6659	
6660	## `whisker-local-store`
6661	
6662	Persistent, string-keyed key-value store. Stateless one-shot operations
6663	namespaced under the unit struct `WhiskerLocalStore`. Backed by
6664	`UserDefaults` (iOS) and `SharedPreferences` (Android); persists across
6665	launches but doesn't sync across devices. For small state — not large
6666	blobs.
6667	
6668	```toml
6669	[dependencies]
6670	whisker-local-store = "0.12"
6671	```
6672	
6673	### `WhiskerLocalStore`
6674	
6675	Associated functions (no instance to construct). Each returns a
6676	`Result<_, WhiskerModuleError>`.
6677	
6678	| Method   | Signature                                                            | Returns                                           |
6679	| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
6680	| `save`   | `fn(key: String, value: String) -> Result<bool, WhiskerModuleError>` | `true` on success. Overwrites any existing value. |
6681	| `load`   | `fn(key: String) -> Result<Option<String>, WhiskerModuleError>`      | `Some(value)`, or `None` when no entry exists.    |
6682	| `remove` | `fn(key: String) -> Result<(), WhiskerModuleError>`                  | `Ok(())`. No-op when the key isn't present.       |
6683	
6684	Call from anywhere the reactive runtime runs — component bodies, event
6685	handlers, or effects.
6686	
6687	```rust
6688	use whisker_local_store::WhiskerLocalStore;
6689	
6690	let _ = WhiskerLocalStore::save("user_id".into(), "abc".into())?;
6691	let loaded = WhiskerLocalStore::load("user_id".into())?;
6692	// -> Some("abc".to_string())
6693	let _ = WhiskerLocalStore::remove("user_id".into())?;
6694	```
6695	
6696	# API Reference: Configuration
6697	
6698	Every Whisker app carries a `whisker.rs` binary whose `main` calls
6699	[`whisker_cng::run`](https://docs.rs/whisker-cng/latest/whisker_cng/fn.run.html).
6700	The closure receives a fresh [`Config::default()`](#config). After the closure
6701	returns, CNG prepares plugins and generates the requested platform projects.
6702	Failures print a diagnostic and exit with status 1. Execution requires CNG's
6703	`generate` feature, enabled by the configuration binary's required feature.

| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compile`                                             | Compile SVG XML to a `Compiled` display list. Returns `Result<Compiled, CompileError>`. |
| `Compiled` / `CompileError`                           | The success value (carries `bytes` + `warnings`) and the error type.                    |
| `Color` / `DisplayListBuilder` / `Transform`          | Lower-level builder pieces for constructing a display list by hand.                     |
| `replay` / `ReplayError` / `Visitor` / `TraceVisitor` | Walk a compiled display list, dispatching ops to a `Visitor`.                           |

Most apps never touch these — use `Svg` (or [`whisker-icons`](#whisker-icons))
instead.

## `whisker-icons`

Lucide icon set as a Whisker component. Each icon is its own
`pub const &str`, so unreferenced icons are linker-DCE'd from your
binary (tree shaking).

```toml
[dependencies]
whisker-icons = "0.12"
```

### `Icon`

A pure component that forwards to [`whisker_svg::Svg`](#whisker-svg).

| Prop    | Type             | Notes                                                                                                                 |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `svg`   | `Signal<String>` | The SVG XML to render — usually a `lucide` constant.                                                                  |
| `color` | `Signal<String>` | CSS color used as the `currentColor` substitution (Lucide draws with `stroke="currentColor"`).                        |
| `size`  | `Signal<String>` | Square edge length. Bare numbers (`"24"`) are treated as `px`; values with a unit (`"1.5em"`, `"100%"`) pass through. |

### `lucide`

A module of ~1700 PascalCase `pub const &str` icon constants
(`Heart`, `ChevronRight`, `Search`, `X`, `AlarmClock`, …), each holding
the full Lucide SVG markup. Reference a constant by name and pass it to
`Icon`'s `svg` prop.

```rust
use whisker_icons::{Icon, lucide};

render! {
    Icon(svg: lucide::Heart, color: "#ff5577", size: "24")
}
```

## `whisker-video`

Video playback element with imperative controls. A native UI element
(`Video`) plus a typed handle (`VideoHandle`) bound on mount via
[`element_ref:`](/docs/refs.md).

```toml
[dependencies]
whisker-video = "0.12"
```

### `Video`

Declared via `#[whisker::module_element(...)]`.

| Prop          | Type             | Notes                                               |
| ------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `src`         | `Signal<String>` | Media URL.                                          |
| `style`       | `Style`          | Structured layout and paint.                        |
| `element_ref` | `ElementRef`     | Pass `handle.r()` to bind a `VideoHandle` on mount. |

### `VideoHandle`

A `Copy` handle wrapping an [`ElementRef`](/docs/refs.md). Each method
dispatches a fire-and-forget call to the native player.

| Method  | Signature                          | Effect                                                    |
| ------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `new`   | `fn() -> VideoHandle`              | Allocate a fresh, unbound handle.                         |
| `r`     | `fn(&self) -> ElementRef`          | The `ElementRef` to pass to `Video(element_ref: …)`.      |
| `play`  | `fn(&self)`                        | Start or resume playback from the current position.       |
| `pause` | `fn(&self)`                        | Pause at the current position.                            |
| `seek`  | `fn(&self, position_seconds: f64)` | Seek to an absolute position (seconds; clamped natively). |

`VideoHandle` is `Copy`, so each `move ||` closure captures its own
copy — no `clone()`.

```rust
use whisker_video::{Video, VideoHandle};

let video = VideoHandle::new();

render! {
    View(style: css!(flex_direction: FlexDirection::Column)) {
        Video(element_ref: video.r(), src: "https://example.com/clip.mp4",
              style: css!(width: percent(100), height: px(240)))
        View(style: css!(flex_direction: FlexDirection::Row)) {
            Text(value: "play",  on_tap: move |_| video.play())
            Text(value: "pause", on_tap: move |_| video.pause())
            Text(value: "+10s",  on_tap: move |_| video.seek(10.0))
        }
    }
}
```

## `whisker-audio`

View-less audio playback. A `Player` handle drives the engine and
exposes a reactive [`PlaybackStatus`](/docs/reactivity-api.md) signal. The
crate also ships a plugin that contributes the iOS/Android permission
and background-mode entries.

```toml
[dependencies]
whisker-audio = "0.12"
```

### `Player`

A `Clone` handle (internally `Rc`-counted); the native player releases
when the last clone drops. Methods are fire-and-forget — state changes
surface through `status()`, not return values.

| Method       | Signature                                 | Effect                                                                          |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `new`        | `fn(source: impl Into<String>) -> Player` | Construct a player loading from `source` (HTTP/HTTPS or `file://`).             |
| `play`       | `fn(&self)`                               | Start or resume playback.                                                       |
| `pause`      | `fn(&self)`                               | Pause at the current position.                                                  |
| `stop`       | `fn(&self)`                               | Stop and rewind to position 0 (stays loaded).                                   |
| `seek_to`    | `fn(&self, position_seconds: f64)`        | Seek to an absolute position (seconds; clamped natively).                       |
| `set_source` | `fn(&self, source: impl Into<String>)`    | Replace the loaded media (resets the player; empty string releases the source). |
| `set_volume` | `fn(&self, value: f64)`                   | Set output gain on `[0.0, 1.0]` (clamped natively).                             |
| `set_loop`   | `fn(&self, looping: bool)`                | Loop the source at end-of-media.                                                |
| `status`     | `fn(&self) -> ReadSignal<PlaybackStatus>` | Reactive playback status. All clones share one signal.                          |

### `PlaybackStatus`

`#[non_exhaustive]` snapshot pushed by the native side (times in
seconds). Read fields directly; construct only via the native module.

| Field        | Type   | Meaning                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `position`   | `f64`  | Current playback position from the start.                               |
| `duration`   | `f64`  | Total media duration. `0.0` while loading or for live streams.          |
| `is_loaded`  | `bool` | `true` once the source headers are parsed and `duration` is meaningful. |
| `is_playing` | `bool` | `true` while audio is actively playing.                                 |

```rust
use whisker_audio::Player;

let player = Player::new("https://example.com/clip.mp3");
let status = player.status();

render! {
    View(style: css!(flex_direction: FlexDirection::Column, padding: px(16))) {
        Text(value: computed(move || format!(
            "{:.1}s / {:.1}s",
            status.get().position,
            status.get().duration,
        )))
        View(on_tap: {
            let p = player.clone();
            move |_| p.play()
        }) { Text(value: "play") }
    }
}
```

### Plugin: `WhiskerAudio` + `WhiskerAudioConfig`

To record audio or keep playback alive in the background, register the
plugin in `whisker.rs` (see [Configuration](/docs/configuration-api.md)).
The plugin contributes the matching `Info.plist` /
`AndroidManifest.xml` entries.

| Config field / setter         | Type             | Effect                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `microphone_permission`       | `Option<String>` | Sets `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` (iOS). Required before `AVAudioSession` can record. |
| `record_audio_android`        | `bool`           | Appends `android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO` to the Android manifest. Default `false`.     |
| `enable_background_recording` | `bool`           | Adds `"audio"` to iOS `UIBackgroundModes`. Default `false`.                             |
| `enable_background_playback`  | `bool`           | Same `UIBackgroundModes` entry, expressing playback intent. Default `false`.            |

```rust
use whisker_audio::WhiskerAudio;

app.plugin::<WhiskerAudio>(|c| c
    .microphone_permission("Record audio clips for podcasts.")
    .record_audio_android(true)
    .enable_background_playback(true));
```

## `whisker-safe-area`

Reactive accessor for the host view's safe-area insets (notch, Dynamic
Island, status bar, home indicator, navigation bar).

```toml
[dependencies]
whisker-safe-area = "0.12"
```

### `safe_area_insets()`

```rust
pub fn safe_area_insets() -> ReadSignal<SafeAreaInsets>
```

Returns a process-global [`ReadSignal`](/docs/reactivity-api.md) wired to
the native event on first call. Every call hands back the same
underlying signal, so reading from many components is cheap. **Must be
called from the main thread.**

### `SafeAreaInsets`

A `Copy` struct of inset amounts in points (iOS) / dp (Android) — the
same units as Whisker's CSS `px` literals.

| Field      | Type  | Meaning                             |
| ---------- | ----- | ----------------------------------- |
| `top`      | `f64` | Top inset.                          |
| `leading`  | `f64` | Leading edge (`== left` for LTR).   |
| `trailing` | `f64` | Trailing edge (`== right` for LTR). |
| `bottom`   | `f64` | Bottom inset.                       |

```rust
use whisker_safe_area::safe_area_insets;

let insets = safe_area_insets();
let outer_style = move || {
    let i = insets.get();
    format!(
        "padding-top: {}px; padding-bottom: {}px; \
         padding-left: {}px; padding-right: {}px;",
        i.top, i.bottom, i.leading, i.trailing,
    )
};

render! {
    View(style: outer_style()) {
        // ...
    }
}
```

## `whisker-local-store`

Persistent, string-keyed key-value store. Stateless one-shot operations
namespaced under the unit struct `WhiskerLocalStore`. Backed by
`UserDefaults` (iOS) and `SharedPreferences` (Android); persists across
launches but doesn't sync across devices. For small state — not large
blobs.

```toml
[dependencies]
whisker-local-store = "0.12"
```

### `WhiskerLocalStore`

Associated functions (no instance to construct). Each returns a
`Result<_, WhiskerModuleError>`.

| Method   | Signature                                                            | Returns                                           |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `save`   | `fn(key: String, value: String) -> Result<bool, WhiskerModuleError>` | `true` on success. Overwrites any existing value. |
| `load`   | `fn(key: String) -> Result<Option<String>, WhiskerModuleError>`      | `Some(value)`, or `None` when no entry exists.    |
| `remove` | `fn(key: String) -> Result<(), WhiskerModuleError>`                  | `Ok(())`. No-op when the key isn't present.       |

Call from anywhere the reactive runtime runs — component bodies, event
handlers, or effects.

```rust
use whisker_local_store::WhiskerLocalStore;

let _ = WhiskerLocalStore::save("user_id".into(), "abc".into())?;
let loaded = WhiskerLocalStore::load("user_id".into())?;
// -> Some("abc".to_string())
let _ = WhiskerLocalStore::remove("user_id".into())?;
```

# API Reference: Configuration

Every Whisker app carries a `whisker.rs` binary whose `main` calls
[`whisker_cng::run`](https://docs.rs/whisker-cng/latest/whisker_cng/fn.run.html).
The closure receives a fresh [`Config::default()`](#config). After the closure
returns, CNG prepares plugins and generates the requested platform projects.
Failures print a diagnostic and exit with status 1. Execution requires CNG's
`generate` feature, enabled by the configuration binary's required feature.
