Stdout is strictly the response envelope; stderr is reserved for human-readable diagnostics. ### `PluginRequest` | Field | Type | Notes | | --------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `name` | `String` | Plugin name the engine is asking for. | | `config` | `serde_json::Value` | The plugin's config as JSON (`null` → `Default`). | | `context` | `GenerateContext` | The IRs going into this plugin. | ### `PluginResponse` | Field | Type | Notes | | --------- | ----------------- | -------------------------- | | `context` | `GenerateContext` | The post-mutation context. | ### `run_as_subprocess` ```rust pub fn run_as_subprocess(plugin: P) -> anyhow::Result<()>; ``` Reads a `PluginRequest` from stdin, asserts the name matches, decodes the config (or uses `Default` when `null`), runs `validate` then `apply`, and writes a `PluginResponse` to stdout. The recommended `main`: ```rust fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> { whisker_plugin::run_as_subprocess(Demo) } ``` A returned error exits with status 1 and the message on stderr — the contract the engine expects. # API Reference: CLI Reference Install the CLI from Cargo: ```sh cargo install whisker-cli ``` The package installs both `whisker` and the `cargo whisker` shim. The examples below use the direct form. ## Global options | Option | Purpose | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | `-v`, `--verbose` | Show raw Cargo, native toolchain, device, and internal logs | | `--no-tui` | Use deterministic line output instead of the interactive TUI | | `--help` | Show the exact options supported by the installed version | The TUI is disabled automatically when output is piped or runs under CI. ## `whisker run` ```sh whisker run android whisker run ios whisker run web whisker run desktop ``` `run` syncs `gen//`, builds, installs or serves the app, launches the Host, watches source files, and applies hot patches when possible. | Option | Default | Purpose | | ------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------- | | `--manifest-path ` | nearest package manifest | Select the app crate | | `--bind ` | `127.0.0.1:9876` | Dev server/Web address | | `--no-hot-patch` | off | Require explicit full reloads | | `--workspace-root ` | discovered | Override the Cargo workspace root | Interactive keys are shown in the TUI. Common actions are `r` for a hot reload, `R` for a full reload, `o` to relaunch/open, and `q` to quit. `desktop` currently launches the macOS Host. The desktop rendering library is shared with Windows and Linux, but their launch shells are not yet exposed by this target. ## `whisker build` ```sh whisker build appbundle whisker build apk whisker build ipa whisker build macos whisker build web ``` The command syncs the same `gen/` project used by `run` and produces a distributable artifact. Android and iOS commands integrate with Whisker's credential store; macOS produces an `.app`; Web produces a static HTML, JavaScript, and WebAssembly bundle. Run `whisker build --help` for signing and output options. Generated Android and iOS projects are ordinary Gradle and Xcode projects. After generation, their IDE or native build command can compile the app without placing `whisker run` around the build. ## `whisker submit` ```sh whisker submit ios whisker submit android ``` `submit` uploads the artifact the last `whisker build` produced to App Store Connect or Google Play. It does not build. If the app has a [`store.rs`](/docs/store-submission.md#declaring-store-metadata-storers), the release notes declared there are sent with the binary. | Option | Applies to | Purpose | | ---------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | `--path ` | both | Upload this artifact instead of the last build's | | `--no-wait` | `ios` | Return without waiting for App Store Connect to process the build | | `--track ` | `android` | Also release on a track; without it the bundle is only uploaded | | `--draft` | `android` | With `--track`, create the release as a draft | ## `whisker store` ```sh whisker store push appstore whisker store push playstore whisker store pull appstore whisker store pull playstore ``` `store push` writes the store page metadata declared in `store.rs`: text, images, categories, and review details. `store pull` prints what a store currently holds as a complete `store.rs` on stdout and changes nothing. | Option | Applies to | Purpose | | ------------------ | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `--dry-run` | `push` | List what would be written without contacting the store | | `--create-version` | `push appstore` | Create the next version from `whisker.rs` when none is being prepared | See [Store Submission](/docs/store-submission.md) for the workflow and [Store Metadata](/docs/store-metadata.md) for everything `store.rs` can declare. ## Scaffolding and diagnostics | Command | Purpose | | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | `whisker new ` | Create an app crate and workspace | | `whisker new-module ` | Create Rust, Swift, Kotlin, Web, and desktop module structure | | `whisker doctor` | Check Rust targets and the Android SDK, NDK, JDK, and Xcode | | `whisker credential ...` | Create, import, or rotate signing and store credentials | | `whisker fmt ...` | Run rustfmt plus Whisker macro formatting | The CLI and the app's `whisker` / `whisker-cng` dependencies must be the same version. After upgrading the CLI, update the app to match (`cargo update -p whisker -p whisker-cng`, or edit `Cargo.toml` across a minor version); `whisker run` stops with both versions and these instructions when they differ. `build-ios`, `build-android`, and `modules` are internal build-system entry points. Generated Xcode/Gradle projects call them; application developers should not invoke them directly. # API Reference: Formatting `whisker fmt` delegates ordinary Rust syntax to rustfmt, then formats the compose-style invocations used by `render!`, `css!`, and `routes!`.

# Plugin registration — Whisker walks the consuming app's dep tree, picks

# every `whisker build` / `whisker run` gen sync. It is unconditional (no

# Subprocess binary entry point. Reads a `PluginRequest` JSON from stdin,
# mutates the IR via `RouterPlugin::apply`, writes a `PluginResponse` JSON.
[[bin]]
name = "whisker-router-plugin"
path = "bin/whisker_router_plugin.rs"
test = false
bench = false
doc = false

[dependencies]
whisker = { path = "../../crates/whisker", version = "0.16.0" }
# Plugin support (trait + IR types + JSON envelope + subprocess runner).
# Light deps so the config-probe build path stays cheap.
whisker-plugin = { path = "../../crates/whisker-plugin", version = "0.16.0" }
serde = { workspace = true }
anyhow = { workspace = true }
# The `routes!` declarative route-tree macro, re-exported below.
whisker-macros = { path = "../../crates/whisker-macros", version = "0.16.0" }

[dev-dependencies]
# Test-only: drive animation frames (`__step_for_tests`) so the
# render-layer tests can advance a push/pop transition to completion and
# assert the wrappers settle to their resting pose.
whisker-animation = { path = "../../crates/whisker-animation", version = "0.16.0" }
whisker-style = { path = "../../crates/whisker-style", version = "0.16.0" }
# Test-only: drive `RouterPlugin` through the real CNG engine + Android

# `enableOnBackInvokedCallback`. No cycle: whisker-cng depends on
# whisker-plugin / whisker-config, never on whisker-router.

whisker-config = { path = "../../crates/whisker-config", version = "0.16.0" }

37:/// ScrollView `scroll` listener. The Host reports geometry with the same
38:/// node event path used by custom elements; no list-specific bridge call

input.content:
# Building Everbloom (Whisker)

All commands run from the project root of a clean checkout, in `bash`/`zsh`.
`gen/` (native projects) and `build/` (Xcode derived data) are generated and
git-ignored.

## 1. Install dependencies

Prerequisites: macOS with Xcode 26 (command line tools selected), Android
Studio (Android SDK, NDK 27.x and its bundled JDK; Whisker finds them under
`~/Library/Android/sdk` without `ANDROID_HOME`/`JAVA_HOME`), and rustup.

```sh
rustup toolchain install stable
rustup target add aarch64-apple-ios aarch64-apple-ios-sim aarch64-linux-android
cargo install whisker-cli --version 0.16.0 --locked
whisker doctor            # every check should pass
cargo fetch               # Rust dependencies (pinned by Cargo.lock)
```

The Swift (SwiftPM) and Android (Gradle/Maven) dependencies are resolved by
`xcodebuild` / Gradle on the first build.

## 2. iOS device release build (benchmarked)

Generate the Xcode project from `whisker.rs`, then build Release for
`generic/platform=iOS` (arm64). The Xcode build phase compiles the Rust crate
in release mode (`whisker build-ios --configuration Release`, `lto = true`,
`codegen-units = 1`); hot reload / the dev server are not part of this build.

```sh
cargo run --bin whisker-config --features whisker-config -- ios
```

Signed, with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set (automatic signing):

```sh
export DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345   # your Apple team ID
xcodebuild -project gen/ios/Everbloom.xcodeproj -scheme Everbloom \
  -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  -derivedDataPath build/device \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
  build
```

Without a team (code signing disabled):

```sh
xcodebuild -project gen/ios/Everbloom.xcodeproj -scheme Everbloom \
  -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  -derivedDataPath build/device \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  build
```

Resulting app: `build/device/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Everbloom.app`

(`-skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation` let a headless build use
Whisker's SwiftPM codegen plugin and Swift macro; `whisker` itself passes the
same flags.)

## 3. Install and launch on a connected iPhone

```sh
xcrun devicectl list devices                     # note the device identifier
DEVICE=<device-identifier>
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$DEVICE" \
  build/device/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Everbloom.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$DEVICE" \
  --terminate-existing \
  --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"http://192.168.1.20:8787/api"}' \
  dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.whisker
```

`SHOP_API_URL` is read at launch; when unset or empty the app uses
`https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`. The `SHOPBENCH home_ready`
marker is written with `NSLog` and appears in Console.app for the device.

## 4. iOS Simulator build (verification)

Mode: **Release configuration** for the simulator (`iphonesimulator` SDK,
`aarch64-apple-ios-sim` Rust target, release Rust profile) — the most
production-like mode Whisker supports there; same generated project as the
device build, no dev server or hot reload.

```sh
cargo run --bin whisker-config --features whisker-config -- ios
xcodebuild -project gen/ios/Everbloom.xcodeproj -scheme Everbloom \
  -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
  -derivedDataPath build/sim \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  build
```

Resulting app: `build/sim/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/Everbloom.app`

Install and launch on the booted simulator, with the endpoint override:

```sh
xcrun simctl install booted build/sim/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/Everbloom.app
SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api \
  xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process booted dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.whisker
# log marker:
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'
```

## 5. Android release APK

Mode: Gradle `release` build type (Rust compiled in release mode for
`arm64-v8a`), signed with the local debug keystore through the
`WHISKER_ANDROID_*` variables the generated Gradle project reads.

The endpoint is a **build-time** setting on Android: export `SHOP_API_URL`
before building (omit it for the default mock.shop endpoint). Cargo tracks the
variable, so changing it rebuilds the Rust library.

```sh
cargo run --bin whisker-config --features whisker-config -- android
export SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api   # optional
cd gen/android && \
  WHISKER_ANDROID_KEYSTORE="$HOME/.android/debug.keystore" \
  WHISKER_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD=android \
  WHISKER_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS=androiddebugkey \
  WHISKER_ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD=android \
  ./gradlew :app:assembleRelease && cd ../..
```

(If `~/.android/debug.keystore` does not exist yet, create it with
`keytool -genkeypair -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore -storepass android -alias androiddebugkey -keypass android -keyalg RSA -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Android Debug,O=Android,C=US"`.)

Resulting APK: `gen/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`

```sh
adb install -r gen/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.whisker/.MainActivity
```

## 6. Build modes and toolchain versions

| Target | Mode |
|---|---|
| iOS device | Xcode `Release`, `generic/platform=iOS` (arm64), Rust release profile with LTO |
| iOS Simulator | Xcode `Release`, `iphonesimulator`, Rust release profile with LTO |
| Android | Gradle `release`, arm64-v8a, Rust release profile with LTO, debug-keystore signing |

Versions used:

- macOS 26.5.1, Xcode 26.6 (17F113), iOS Simulator runtime 26.5 (iPhone 17 Pro)
- Rust 1.96.0 (stable), cargo 1.96.0
- Whisker 0.16.0 (`whisker`, `whisker-cli`, `whisker-cng`, `whisker-plugin`),
  whisker-router 0.14.3, whisker-image / -svg / -input / -keyboard /
  -safe-area / -web-browser 0.14.4; Whisker iOS SwiftPM package 0.1.19,
  Android SDK artifacts 0.1.21/0.1.26
- Gradle 8.11.1 (wrapper), JDK 21.0.6 (Android Studio JBR), Android
  compileSdk 34 / minSdk 24 / targetSdk 34, NDK 27.x
- Android emulator: `Medium_Phone` AVD

# Notes

## Project layout

- `src/lib.rs`: entry point, router (tabs layout + per-tab stacks), tab bar, cart badge.
- `src/api.rs`: GraphQL documents (copied verbatim from `spec/storefront.graphql`), models, transport.
- `src/state.rs`: in-memory cart (`AppState`, provided through context).
- `src/ui.rs`: design tokens, icons, shared components (product card, price, skeletons, spinner, error state, nav bar).
- `src/screens/`: Home, Collection, Product, Search, Cart.
- `shop-native/`: app-private Whisker module (Swift + Kotlin) and generation plugin, see below.
- `whisker.rs`: app configuration (name, bundle id, portrait-only iOS, white background).

## Dependencies added

Rust crates (app):

- `whisker`, `whisker-cng`: the framework and its project generator (required by every Whisker app).
- `whisker-router`: first-party navigation (tabs + stacks, back gesture).
- `whisker-image`: first-party network image element (aspect-fill, caching).
- `whisker-svg`: first-party vector rendering for the design's icons.
- `whisker-input`: first-party native text field (search).
- `whisker-keyboard`: first-party keyboard height / dismiss (search results stay above the keyboard; drag dismisses it).
- `whisker-safe-area`: first-party safe-area insets.
- `whisker-web-browser`: first-party in-app browser (SFSafariViewController / Custom Tabs) for Check out.
- `serde`, `serde_json`: JSON encoding/decoding of GraphQL requests and responses. Whisker itself already depends on both, so they add no new code to the binary.

`shop-native` (local module) build-time-only crates: `whisker-plugin` (Whisker's plugin API), `anyhow` (required by the `Plugin` trait signature). They are used by the generation plugin binary, not by the app at runtime.

No third-party UI kit, state library, GraphQL client, or HTTP client. No third-party native (Swift/Kotlin) dependencies were added beyond what the first-party Whisker modules bring (Kingfisher via `whisker-image` on iOS, Coil on Android, androidx.browser via `whisker-web-browser`).

## Why a local module (`shop-native`)

Whisker has no HTTP client, timer, alert, or system-log API. Rather than adding Rust HTTP/TLS crates, the app uses the platform's own facilities through a small Whisker module:

- `post` (async): HTTP POST with URLSession (iOS) / HttpURLConnection (Android). All GraphQL requests go through it.
- `sleep` (async): main-loop timer, used for the 300 ms search debounce.
- `alert`: native alert (UIAlertController / AlertDialog) for cart `userErrors` and failed cart requests.
- `log`: `NSLog` (iOS unified log) / `Log.i` (Android) — used only for the single `SHOPBENCH home_ready` line.
- `tagTextField` (iOS): sets `search-input` as the accessibility identifier of the native `UITextField`, because `whisker-input` does not expose the common `accessibility` prop, and the identifier must be on the text field itself for `app.textFields["search-input"]`.
- Generation plugin (auto-discovered, like `whisker-router`'s): adds `NSAppTransportSecurity` (`NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`, `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`) and `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone = true` to Info.plist. Android's generated manifest already sets `usesCleartextTraffic="true"`.

## Decisions where the spec is silent

- **Endpoint**: iOS reads `SHOP_API_URL` from the process environment at launch; otherwise the value of `SHOP_API_URL` at build time (Android); otherwise the default endpoint.
- **GraphQL documents**: each request sends its operation followed by the fragment definitions it spreads (`ProductCard` / `CartFields`), text unchanged from the spec file, so the document is valid. Responses with a non-empty top-level `errors` are treated as failures.
- **Routes**: `Product` is declared in both the Home and Search stacks, so each tab keeps its own history. Product and Collection screens are pushed (`push`), so a recommendation always adds a new Product screen. The tab bar is hidden whenever the current route is a Product screen.
- **Tab re-selection**: tapping the already-active tab pops that tab to its root (Whisker router default `PopToRoot`). Switching to another tab keeps each tab's stack.
- **Add to cart**: switches to the Cart tab only when the mutation succeeds with no `userErrors`. The button is disabled (50% opacity, taps ignored) while any cart mutation is in flight.
- **Quantity stepper**: one cart mutation at a time; taps while a mutation is in flight are ignored and the stepper is dimmed. Quantity and line total come from the server response.
- **Variant selection**: picks the variant matching the current options with the tapped value; if no exact match exists, the first variant having that value.
- **Price on cards**: `priceRange.minVariantPrice`, with `compareAtPriceRange.minVariantPrice` struck through when higher (also used for search rows and recommendations).
- **Collection header**: nav bar, description, and sort chips stay fixed; only the grid scrolls (`product-grid`). The nav-bar title shows the title from Home immediately and is replaced by the API title.
- **Infinite scroll**: the next page is requested when the scroll position is within one viewport height of the end (from `List`'s scroll events, with `on_end_reached` as a fallback). Failed next-page requests are silently retried on the next scroll.
- **Search**: an empty (or whitespace-only) field immediately shows the hint and cancels any in-flight query; other input is debounced by 300 ms. Stale responses are dropped with a generation counter. The results count is fixed above the list. The keyboard is dismissed when the results are dragged or Search is pressed, and the screen shrinks above the keyboard.
- **Loading states**: Home, Product, and Collection show skeletons; Search's first page and the next-page footer show a small rotating ring (CSS keyframe animation — the only animation in the app besides the router's default transitions).
- **Errors**: Home, Collection, Product, and Search show the design's error state with Retry. Cart request failures show an alert.
- **Empty cart**: the design's "Start shopping" button switches to the Home tab.
- **Design "See all" link** (Collections header): not implemented — the spec does not define a destination, and it says not to add features.
- **Accessibility**: tappable cards/buttons have role button plus a label; containers (`cart-line-<i>`, `home-scroll`, `product-grid`, `search-results`, `product-carousel`) carry only an identifier, so their children stay reachable. The cart badge is a sibling of the Cart tab button (not a child), so it stays its own element, labeled with the count. The router keeps covered screens mounted; a wrapper hides covered screens from accessibility (computed under the never-paused tab-layout owner) so identifiers such as `back` and `add-to-cart` are unique.
- **Orientation**: iOS is portrait-only via `whisker.rs`. Whisker's config has no Android orientation setting, so Android is not locked (no landscape layout is provided).
- **Launch screen**: Whisker's generated launch screen with the `#FFFFFF` app background. No app icon is configured.
- **Release profile**: `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1` for smaller, faster release binaries.

## Spec items not fully met / caveats

- **Device signing** was not exercised (no Apple team available here). The device build is verified with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`; the signed command follows Whisker's documented approach (`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` + `CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic` on the `xcodebuild` command line).
- **Android orientation** is not locked to portrait (see above).
- **Android endpoint override** is build-time only, as the spec allows.
- **`search-input` on iOS** is applied natively after the Search screen mounts (it retries for up to 2 s). On Android the search field has no test tag.

# Notes

## Project layout

- `src/lib.rs`: entry point, router (tabs layout + per-tab stacks), tab bar, cart badge.
- `src/api.rs`: GraphQL documents (copied verbatim from `spec/storefront.graphql`), models, transport.
- `src/state.rs`: in-memory cart (`AppState`, provided through context).
- `src/ui.rs`: design tokens, icons, shared components (product card, price, skeletons, spinner, error state, nav bar).
- `src/screens/`: Home, Collection, Product, Search, Cart.
- `shop-native/`: app-private Whisker module (Swift + Kotlin) and generation plugin, see below.
- `whisker.rs`: app configuration (name, bundle id, portrait-only iOS, white background).

## Dependencies added

Rust crates (app):

- `whisker`, `whisker-cng`: the framework and its project generator (required by every Whisker app).
- `whisker-router`: first-party navigation (tabs + stacks, back gesture).
- `whisker-image`: first-party network image element (aspect-fill, caching).
- `whisker-svg`: first-party vector rendering for the design's icons.
- `whisker-input`: first-party native text field (search).
- `whisker-keyboard`: first-party keyboard height / dismiss (search results stay above the keyboard; drag dismisses it).
- `whisker-safe-area`: first-party safe-area insets.
- `whisker-web-browser`: first-party in-app browser (SFSafariViewController / Custom Tabs) for Check out.
- `serde`, `serde_json`: JSON encoding/decoding of GraphQL requests and responses. Whisker itself already depends on both, so they add no new code to the binary.

`shop-native` (local module) build-time-only crates: `whisker-plugin` (Whisker's plugin API), `anyhow` (required by the `Plugin` trait signature). They are used by the generation plugin binary, not by the app at runtime.

No third-party UI kit, state library, GraphQL client, or HTTP client. No third-party native (Swift/Kotlin) dependencies were added beyond what the first-party Whisker modules bring (Kingfisher via `whisker-image` on iOS, Coil on Android, androidx.browser via `whisker-web-browser`).

## Why a local module (`shop-native`)

Whisker has no HTTP client, timer, alert, or system-log API. Rather than adding Rust HTTP/TLS crates, the app uses the platform's own facilities through a small Whisker module:

- `post` (async): HTTP POST with URLSession (iOS) / HttpURLConnection (Android). All GraphQL requests go through it.
- `sleep` (async): main-loop timer, used for the 300 ms search debounce.
- `alert`: native alert (UIAlertController / AlertDialog) for cart `userErrors` and failed cart requests.
- `log`: `NSLog` (iOS unified log) / `Log.i` (Android) — used only for the single `SHOPBENCH home_ready` line.
- `tagTextField` (iOS): sets `search-input` as the accessibility identifier of the native `UITextField`, because `whisker-input` does not expose the common `accessibility` prop, and the identifier must be on the text field itself for `app.textFields["search-input"]`.
- Generation plugin (auto-discovered, like `whisker-router`'s): adds `NSAppTransportSecurity` (`NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`, `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`) and `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone = true` to Info.plist. Android's generated manifest already sets `usesCleartextTraffic="true"`.

## Decisions where the spec is silent

- **Endpoint**: iOS reads `SHOP_API_URL` from the process environment at launch; otherwise the value of `SHOP_API_URL` at build time (Android); otherwise the default endpoint.
- **GraphQL documents**: each request sends its operation followed by the fragment definitions it spreads (`ProductCard` / `CartFields`), text unchanged from the spec file, so the document is valid. Responses with a non-empty top-level `errors` are treated as failures.
- **Routes**: `Product` is declared in both the Home and Search stacks, so each tab keeps its own history. Product and Collection screens are pushed (`push`), so a recommendation always adds a new Product screen. The tab bar is hidden whenever the current route is a Product screen.
- **Tab re-selection**: tapping the already-active tab pops that tab to its root (Whisker router default `PopToRoot`). Switching to another tab keeps each tab's stack.
- **Add to cart**: switches to the Cart tab only when the mutation succeeds with no `userErrors`. The button is disabled (50% opacity, taps ignored) while any cart mutation is in flight.
- **Quantity stepper**: one cart mutation at a time; taps while a mutation is in flight are ignored and the stepper is dimmed. Quantity and line total come from the server response.
- **Variant selection**: picks the variant matching the current options with the tapped value; if no exact match exists, the first variant having that value.
- **Price on cards**: `priceRange.minVariantPrice`, with `compareAtPriceRange.minVariantPrice` struck through when higher (also used for search rows and recommendations).
- **Collection header**: nav bar, description, and sort chips stay fixed; only the grid scrolls (`product-grid`). The nav-bar title shows the title from Home immediately and is replaced by the API title.
- **Infinite scroll**: the next page is requested when the scroll position is within one viewport height of the end (from `List`'s scroll events, with `on_end_reached` as a fallback). Failed next-page requests are silently retried on the next scroll.
- **Search**: an empty (or whitespace-only) field immediately shows the hint and cancels any in-flight query; other input is debounced by 300 ms. Stale responses are dropped with a generation counter. The results count is fixed above the list. The keyboard is dismissed when the results are dragged or Search is pressed, and the screen shrinks above the keyboard.
- **Loading states**: Home, Product, and Collection show skeletons; Search's first page and the next-page footer show a small rotating ring (CSS keyframe animation — the only animation in the app besides the router's default transitions).
- **Errors**: Home, Collection, Product, and Search show the design's error state with Retry. Cart request failures show an alert.
- **Empty cart**: the design's "Start shopping" button switches to the Home tab.
- **Design "See all" link** (Collections header): not implemented — the spec does not define a destination, and it says not to add features.
- **Accessibility**: tappable cards/buttons have role button plus a label; containers (`cart-line-<i>`, `home-scroll`, `product-grid`, `search-results`, `product-carousel`) carry only an identifier, so their children stay reachable. The cart badge is a sibling of the Cart tab button (not a child), so it stays its own element, labeled with the count. The router keeps covered screens mounted; a wrapper hides covered screens from accessibility (computed under the never-paused tab-layout owner) so identifiers such as `back` and `add-to-cart` are unique.
- **Orientation**: iOS is portrait-only via `whisker.rs`. Whisker's config has no Android orientation setting, so Android is not locked (no landscape layout is provided).
- **Launch screen**: Whisker's generated launch screen with the `#FFFFFF` app background. No app icon is configured.
- **Release profile**: `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1` for smaller, faster release binaries.

## Spec items not fully met / caveats

- **Device signing** was not exercised (no Apple team available here). The device build is verified with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`; the signed command follows Whisker's documented approach (`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` + `CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic` on the `xcodebuild` command line).
- **Android orientation** is not locked to portrait (see above).
- **Android endpoint override** is build-time only, as the spec allows.
- **`search-input` on iOS** is applied natively after the Search screen mounts (it retries for up to 2 s). On Android the search field has no test tag.

content.text:
I built the Everbloom app with Whisker 0.16 in the project root, and it passes every item on the Done checklist I could check here. The one thing I couldn't test is device code signing, because there's no Apple team on this machine. The device build compiles with signing disabled, and the signed command is in `BUILD.md`.

**What I checked**
- **iOS Simulator (Release build):** I drove the installed app with an XCUITest harness I built in the scratchpad.
  - Home loads.
  - A collection opens and scrolls to the end (84 products, loaded 24 at a time), and all four sorts reorder it.
  - Search returns "67 results" and scrolls to the last one.
  - A product opens, its option pills switch the variant, and a recommendation opens another product with the back button returning to the first.
  - Add to cart switches to the Cart tab and shows the badge. The stepper moves the badge 1→2→1 and the subtotal $75→$150→$75. Going to 0 removes the line and shows the empty-cart state.
  - Check out opens the checkout URL in the in-app Safari view.
- **Accessibility identifiers:** they show up in the XCUITest tree, and the ones the flow uses resolve to a single element. `search-input` is on the native text field itself.
- **Log marker:** `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears exactly once per launch in the simulator log stream.
- **Error state:** pointed at an unreachable plain-HTTP endpoint through `SHOP_API_URL`, Home shows "Couldn't load products". After I started a local proxy, Retry loaded Home. This also confirms the endpoint override and plain HTTP work.
- **iOS device:** the Release arm64 build succeeds with signing disabled (5.3 MB `.app`). The Info.plist has the 120 Hz key and the plain-HTTP permission.
- **Android:** a signed release APK installs and runs on the emulator, and Home loads.

**Decisions worth knowing**
- **Small native module (`shop-native/`):** Whisker has no HTTP client, timer, alert or system log, so I wrote one in Swift and Kotlin using the platforms' own HTTP. It also adds the Info.plist keys at generation time. Apart from Whisker's own crates, the only added dependencies are `serde`/`serde_json`, which Whisker already pulls in.
- **Covered screens hidden from accessibility:** Whisker's router keeps the screens underneath mounted. Without a fix, `back` and `add-to-cart` matched twice after opening a product from a recommendation. A wrapper now hides covered screens, so each identifier matches one element.
- **Search screen:** the results shrink above the keyboard, and dragging them dismisses it. Without this, swipes on `search-results` while the keyboard was up started under the keyboard and didn't scroll.
- **Left out or not met:** I didn't implement the design's "See all" link, because the spec gives it no destination. Android isn't locked to portrait, because Whisker's configuration has no setting for it.

All the spec-silent choices and every dependency are listed in `NOTES.md`. `BUILD.md` has the clean-checkout commands, output paths, build modes and toolchain versions.
